article_title: Predicting academic performance with fuzzy logic in prospective physical education and sports teachers.
citation: Anapalı Şenel, A., Göksu, B., Şenel, E., & Solmaz, F. İ. (2025). Predicting academic performance with fuzzy logic in prospective physical education and sports teachers. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-99124-3
title: Teacher Qualification Test for Physical Education (TQT-PE) as the outcome assessment
description: The TQT-PE is the standardised professional qualification exam whose scores the study predicts. It is "a meticulously crafted assessment tool, informed by experts and academicians", covering topics from fundamentals of physical education and sports (13%, 11 questions) to anatomy and kinesiology, health and first aid, exercise physiology, training science, adaptive practices, and team sports (8%, six questions). Topic weightings are set under guidelines established by the Student Selection and Placement Centre (ÖSYM).
requirements: Administered on a pre-determined date to candidates seeking teaching qualification
constraints: The article notes this metric "may not fully reflect broader academic or professional competencies"
target_learners: Prospective physical education and sports teachers
target_learning_goals: Assessing field knowledge and preparedness for physical education teaching roles
examples: The test includes sections such as Fundamentals of Physical Education and Sports (13%), Human Anatomy and Kinesiology (5%), and Team Sports (8%)
key_sources: Anapalı Şenel, A., Göksu, B., Şenel, E., & Solmaz, F. İ. (2025). Predicting academic performance with fuzzy logic in prospective physical education and sports teachers. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-99124-3

article_title: Exploring Gamification in Quantum Computing: The Qubit Factory
citation: Glen Evenbly. (2024). Exploring Gamification in Quantum Computing: The Qubit Factory. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11995
title: Geometric visual language for representing quantum states and gates in TQF
description: TQF introduces a custom visual language for quantum states and circuits: single-qubit states are arrows on a 2D disk (possible because only real-valued wavefunctions are allowed), superpositions are shown by qubits 'blinking' between basis states with amplitude magnitude indicated by dash length and time spent in each state, and entanglement is signified by color-matched translucent clouds sized by single-qubit entanglement entropy. Gates are designed so their function can be inferred visually, e.g. the flip gate shows a reflection about its axis. The article notes "the magnitude of each amplitude in the superposition is indicated both by the amount of time spent in the basis state and also by the length of the dashes along the edge of the qubit disk". A state analyzer supplements these visuals with precise amplitude, entropy, and measurement-probability information.
requirements: Restriction to real-valued wavefunctions, which allows a single qubit state to be represented as an arrow on a 2D disk rather than in the 3D Bloch sphere
A state analyzer for states too complicated to convey by blinking alone
constraints: The article states blinking representations are "undoubtedly inadequate to describe more complicated states", requiring the state analyzer as a supplement
target_learners: Users without a prior education in quantum theory
target_learning_goals: Visualizing quantum states, superpositions, and entanglement
Inferring the function of quantum gates without memorizing notation
examples: A GHZ state on four qubits is depicted as blinking between the two non-zero-amplitude basis states, with color-matched clouds marking the entangled qubits
key_sources: Glen Evenbly. (2024). Exploring Gamification in Quantum Computing: The Qubit Factory. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.11995
